drivingQuestion: Is a fish kosher when it lacks scales now but will grow them, or has them and sheds them on being drawn from the water?
outcomeNote: The unit only adduces the mishna's fish clause and the opening of a baraita on it; the baraita's second clause is cut off at כגון and continues beyond this unit.

segments.he: וּבַדָּגִים כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׂקֶשֶׂת. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו וְעָתִיד לְגַדֵּל לְאַחַר זְמַן, כְּגוֹן הַסּוּלְתָּנִית וְהָעַפְיָאן – הֲרֵי זֶה מוּתָּר. יֵשׁ לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו וְעָתִיד לְהַשִּׁירָן בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעוֹלֶה מִן הַמַּיִם, כְּגוֹן
segments.en: § The mishna states: «And with regard to fish, any» fish «that has a fin and a scale» is kosher. «The Sages taught» in a baraita: If a fish «does not have» scales «now but will grow» them «after» a period of «time, such as the sultanit and afyan» fish, «it is permitted.» Likewise, if «it has» scales «now but will shed them when it» is caught and «rises from the water, such as»
